entries.title: Embedded widgets meet WCAG 2.2 AA and grow with your page
entries.summary: Every embedded widget (agenda, schedule, sessions, speakers, speaker gallery, rooms, content gallery and Ask) works with a keyboard and a screen reader, keeps readable contrast on your colors, and reflows when visitors zoom. Widgets now **grow with their content** instead of scrolling inside a one-screen box; add **`fixed-height`** to keep the box. A widget **inside an iframe** keeps the box automatically. The event name is an **`<h2>`**; set **`heading-level`** to change it.

where.path: Publish → Embeds → embed code on the customer's website

entries.use_case: An organization with an accessibility requirement (public agencies, associations, medical societies) can put the agenda on its site and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

cs_action.note: This changed two defaults without 30 days' notice (one-off exception, Josh, 2026-11-06). A customer whose page was built around the one-screen box should add fixed-height; one whose CSS targets the widget's h1 should add heading-level="1". Widgets in an iframe keep the box automatically (embeds#130).

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the agenda is now much longer on their page, the heading looks different, or asks about accessibility of the embeds.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with embeds on their website; especially accessibility-conscious associations and public bodies.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Embeds → open the embed → copy the embed code; attributes go on the <sessionboard-embed> tag
internal.gotchas: fixed-height still grows when the window is shorter than 600 px, except inside an iframe. heading-level only changes the event name; section titles are one level below it.
internal.talk_track: Your agenda embed is now accessible to keyboard and screen-reader users and reflows when people zoom; if you prefer the old scrolling box, it's one attribute.

entries.title: The Awards Form Builder no longer loses questions
entries.summary: Leaving the Form Builder with unsaved changes, through the sidebar, the top bar or the organization and event switcher, now asks you to **Save and leave**, **Leave without saving** or **Stay on this step**. An old tab can no longer overwrite questions another admin saved: its save is refused with **This form was changed somewhere else**. Removed questions can be recovered, and the Customize Question button now reads **Apply**.

where.path: Awards → program → Settings → Form Builder

entries.use_case: Two program admins building the same nomination form no longer lose each other's questions, and nobody loses a batch of questions by switching events before saving.

cs_action.note: If a customer lost questions before this fix (Informa CPHI did on Nov 3 and Nov 4), questions removed after the release can be restored from the database; earlier hard deletes need a backup.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports questions disappearing from an Awards form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers with several admins editing forms.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Settings → Form Builder (step 3)
internal.gotchas: Customize Question → Apply only updates the page; the footer Save keeps the change.
internal.talk_track: The Form Builder now asks before you leave with unsaved changes and refuses to overwrite a colleague's newer version.

entries.title: Video submissions buffer far less in the Review portal
entries.summary: Large or high-resolution video submissions get a copy made for streaming (up to 720p) the first time a reviewer opens them. Once the copy is ready, playback buffers far less on an ordinary connection; until then, or if the copy can't load, the original plays. **Download** still gives the original file.

where.path: Program Site → My Reviews → open a submission → click a video file

entries.use_case: Programs that collect video abstracts can have reviewers watch them straight through on hotel, hospital or home Wi-Fi instead of waiting for the video to buffer.

cs_action.note: Copies are made automatically the first time a submission is opened. Engineering can pre-build copies for an event that is already in review (scripts/sb-11345-queue-playback-renditions.js); ask in #product-development.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports reviewers seeing videos pause, stutter or load slowly, or is collecting video abstracts or video award entries.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer whose review plans include video file fields — medical and scientific societies with video abstract programs first.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Reviewers → ⋯ → Preview as reviewer in portal → open a submission with a video file
internal.gotchas: The very first open of a video that has no copy yet still plays the original while the copy is made (one to two minutes for a typical 5–10 minute video). Light videos that already stream well play as uploaded, with no note.
internal.talk_track: Your reviewers now get a streaming copy of each video, so it plays smoothly; the original is always one click away with Download.

entries.title: Wrapped: personalised year-in-review story pages for attendees and speakers
entries.summary: Attendees and speakers each receive a personal **Wrapped** story page — opened from their Wrapped email with no login required — that recaps their event in a scroll-snap, on-brand format. Attendees see their numbers, top topics, favourite speaker, clips and what's next; speakers see room counts, hours on stage, saves, clip views, their sessions and key quotes. The final card lets recipients share to LinkedIn, X, Facebook, email, or copy a link, and every share is counted so the organiser can track results. Organizers configure the **Wrapped** campaign in **Marketing → Campaigns**, choosing who gets one (attendees, speakers), which cards appear, sharing permissions, and the next-event links; a live per-person **preview as** panel shows exactly what each recipient will see.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Wrapped; then Marketing → Campaigns → New campaign → Wrapped

where.path: Marketing → Campaigns → Wrapped campaign

entries.use_case: After an event closes, send every attendee and speaker a beautiful, personalised recap of their experience — their numbers, moments and clips — and let them share it on LinkedIn and other networks, turning each person into an organic promoter of your event and driving registrations for the next one.

cs_action.note: The Wrapped campaign kind is behind a super-user flag on both the API (web-api#5203) and the UI. Nothing is visible to customers until both PRs reach production and the feature is enabled for the org. Do not surface to customers until web-api#5203 is live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: After a large event wraps, especially when the customer wants post-event social amplification or is promoting a next event to the same audience.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running conferences or multi-session events with attendee and speaker data, clips, and a Brand Kit set up — particularly those already using Advocacy or Dispatch.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Campaigns → New campaign → Wrapped (visible only to super-users until GA)
internal.gotchas: UI is merged but fully staff-gated; the API PR (web-api#5203) must also be in production before anything works for real. No end-to-end test against a live API has been run yet. LinkedIn sharing copies the post text to the clipboard rather than pre-filling LinkedIn's composer. The Enterprise 'Rewatch' card is locked on card plans. Brand Kit colours and fonts must be configured on the event for the page to match the event's look; otherwise it falls back to the demo palette.
internal.talk_track: Once your event is over, Wrapped sends every attendee and speaker a personal story page — their numbers, clips and highlights — that they can share on LinkedIn in one tap. Each share is tracked, so you can see who amplified your event and how many clicks came back. It's a great way to keep the conversation going and drive early registrations for next year.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers the Wrapped campaign type, the /wrapped/:token story page, the /wrapped/s/:slug public shared page, or the per-person admin preview. A new guide (or a section in the Advocacy guide) should document how to create and configure a Wrapped campaign, what each card shows for attendees vs. speakers, how sharing works (including the LinkedIn clipboard behaviour), what the public shared page reveals, and how to read Wrapped results.
draft.why_use_it: Wrapped turns each attendee's and speaker's event data into a personal, shareable story page styled with your event's Brand Kit. It gives people a memorable way to reflect on what they experienced and makes it easy for them to share that story publicly, extending your event's reach long after the closing session. Organisers control which cards appear, what the shared public page reveals, and which next-event links are promoted, so every share works toward your goals.

entries.title: Scheduler improve mode: results banner, regenerate from scratch, topics guard, and 90-day error
entries.summary: When the Scheduler agent re-generates a draft that already has placed sessions, it now improves the current agenda rather than starting over. A hint under the **Generate** button reads *"Generating again improves the current agenda. Only pinned sessions stay where they are."* A new **Regenerate from scratch** outline button lets organizers explicitly discard all placements, with an inline confirm step (*"Every unpinned session can move."*). After an improve run, the **Explain** tab shows a results banner with before/after scores, sessions moved, re-placed, and placed counts — or a *"No improvements found"* message. Run warnings (pinned sessions with no time, outside the grid, misaligned, overlapping, etc.) appear in an amber block below the banner. **Avoid Parallel Topics** is automatically disabled with an explanatory message when the event has no topic taxonomy. Events spanning more than 90 days now show a clear error toast instead of a generic failure.

where.path: Sessions → Agenda → Scheduler → Draft panel (Generate / Regenerate from scratch); Sessions → Agenda → Scheduler → Explain tab (results banner)

entries.use_case: When an organizer has already run the Scheduler and wants to refine the agenda without losing all their work, they can re-generate to incrementally improve placements — or explicitly choose to start from scratch when a full reshuffle is needed. The results banner and warnings make it clear exactly what changed and why some pinned sessions were left in place.

cs_action.note: Depends on web-api#5204 being live in PROD-US before this UI ships. Plain Generate continues to work against older APIs; only Regenerate from scratch would fail if the API is not yet updated.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has already run the Scheduler once and wants to refine the agenda without starting over, or when they ask why re-generating moved all their sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Sessions 2.0 add-on who use the Scheduler agent for agenda building.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Agenda → Scheduler → Draft panel
internal.gotchas: Do not merge or demo until web-api#5204 is live in PROD-US. The 90-day error toast and the disabled Topics rule are covered by unit tests only — not verified in a live browser against a real long event or a topics-disabled org.
internal.talk_track: If you re-run the Scheduler on a draft that already has sessions placed, it now improves what's there instead of wiping it. You can see exactly what moved and why in the Explain tab, and if you ever do want a full reshuffle, there's a Regenerate from scratch button with a confirm step so you don't do it by accident.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section covering improve mode: what happens when Generate is clicked on a draft with existing placements, how to use Regenerate from scratch, how to read the results banner (scores, moved/re-placed/placed counts, no-improvements state), and what each pinned-session warning code means.
draft.why_use_it: The Scheduler agent builds and refines a draft agenda automatically, moving sessions into the best available slots based on your rules and constraints. Improve mode lets you iterate on an existing draft — tightening the schedule run by run — without discarding manual pins or accepted placements. The results banner and warning list give you full visibility into every decision the scheduler made, so you can trust the output and act on any issues before publishing.

entries.title: WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility improvements across public forms, admin app and self-serve sign-up
entries.summary: A comprehensive WCAG 2.2 AA remediation pass improves keyboard navigation, screen-reader support and colour contrast across the entire product. Highlights include: every form question is now properly labelled with linked error messages and an **Error Summary** that takes focus on submission; the **CFP / abstract form** step indicator is an ordered list with current-step and completion state announced; the **Form Builder** exposes **Move up / Move down** menu items on every question row so drag-and-drop is no longer required; 14 record side panels are now modal dialogs with focus trapping and Escape-to-close; all 32 chart views include a named image, summary and **View data as table** option; a **Schedule…** button on each session in the schedule sidebar removes the need to drag; single-key shortcuts can be turned off under **Account settings → Accessibility**; status badges, track pills and avatars now choose text colour automatically to meet WCAG contrast requirements against any customer brand colour; and PDF posters and contracts expose a text layer for assistive technology.

where.path: All public forms and pages; Admin app (all modules); Account settings → Accessibility (shortcut toggle)

entries.use_case: Any attendee, speaker or reviewer who uses a keyboard, screen reader or other assistive technology can now navigate forms, the admin grid, the schedule builder and all charts without barriers. Organizers who must meet institutional or legal accessibility requirements (such as universities running CFP forms) can point to WCAG 2.2 AA conformance across the platform.

cs_action.note: All changes are default-on and require no configuration. The single-key shortcut toggle is self-serve under Account settings → Accessibility.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer mentions accessibility requirements, VPAT requests, institutional procurement rules, or has speakers/attendees who rely on assistive technology.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers, especially higher-education, government and enterprise accounts that face WCAG or Section 508 compliance requirements.
internal.staff_path: Account settings → Accessibility (shortcut toggle only; all other changes are automatic)
internal.gotchas: The audit noted a small number of remaining items not in this PR (self-serve workspace frame, heading order on 9 admin pages, two agenda targets at 320 px, captions upload UI, email-builder accessibility warnings, brand-colour contrast warnings, Site image alt prompts). Do not promise full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance on those specific surfaces yet.
internal.talk_track: This release closes the vast majority of findings from a full WCAG 2.2 AA audit — axe violations on admin pages dropped from 1,214 nodes to 20, and public-form critical/serious violations went from 60 to 13. If your organisation has accessibility requirements or a VPAT process, this is a significant milestone.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should be expanded beyond registration to cover the platform-wide WCAG 2.2 AA improvements: keyboard navigation in the admin grid and schedule builder, the Move up/Move down alternatives to drag-and-drop in the Form Builder, the Accessibility preferences in Account settings (shortcut toggle), chart data-table fallbacks, and automatic contrast-safe badge colours.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's accessible registration and form experience lets every participant — regardless of how they interact with a computer — complete submissions, review sessions and manage their portal tasks. Keyboard users can navigate complex controls like searchable dropdowns, multi-step forms and the schedule builder without a mouse, and screen readers receive accurate labels, live announcements and focus management at every step. Colour contrast is enforced automatically against any brand palette, so organizers do not need to audit badge and status colours themselves.

entries.title: Send personalised "Wrapped" recap campaigns to attendees and speakers
entries.summary: A new **Wrapped** campaign kind lets organizers send each attendee or speaker a personalised, branded recap page built from their real event data — minutes attended, sessions, quotes, clips, and next-event picks. Speakers get their own edition covering people in the room, co-speakers, key points, and clip performance. Each recipient can share their page to LinkedIn, X, Facebook, or email via a public link that records clicks; a **Preview** step shows who gets which edition and what their page looks like before anything sends.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Wrapped; then Marketing → Campaigns → New Campaign → Wrapped

where.path: Marketing → Campaigns → Wrapped

entries.use_case: After an event closes, send every attendee and speaker a personalised recap that shows exactly what they experienced — time spent, sessions, quotes, and clips — so they leave with a memorable, shareable moment that drives word-of-mouth and re-engagement for the next event.

cs_action.note: Wrapped is staff-only (INTENTS.wrapped.staff_only gate). Non-super users cannot draft or launch it. CSM must enable it per org before the campaign kind appears.

internal.when_to_bring_up: After a large event wraps, especially when the customer has Signals check-in data, clips, and approved quotes — the more data, the richer each page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running multi-session events with Attend check-in, Media/Clips, and Quotes active; enterprise contracts get the 'Rewatch what you missed' card, Marketing Card subscribers do not.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Campaigns → New Campaign → Wrapped; preview at Marketing → Engagement → Wrapped → [campaign] → Preview
internal.gotchas: Pages are only generated for people with real data; anyone with withdrawn consent is excluded and never counted in anyone's rank. The 'Rewatch' card is enterprise-only (contract org, not Marketing Card subscription). Share-card rendering requires Chromium in the API image — confirm it is present in the deployment. The UI PR (web-ui-v2) must also ship before customers can interact with the feature in-browser.
internal.talk_track: After your event, instead of a generic thank-you email, every attendee gets a page that says 'You spent 4 hours 20 minutes learning, heard Sarah Chen speak three times, and were in the top 25% of engaged attendees' — and they can share it to LinkedIn in one click.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no guide for Wrapped campaigns; a new guide should cover creating and launching a Wrapped campaign, the attendee vs. speaker editions, what data each card requires, the Preview step, sharing mechanics (public slug, Open Graph card, click tracking), consent and privacy rules, and the enterprise-only Rewatch card.
draft.why_use_it: Wrapped turns each person's event data into a branded, shareable story — their sessions, minutes, quotes, and clips — delivered as a personal page. Attendees see their engagement highlights and next-event picks; speakers see their audience reach, co-speakers, and clip performance. Because every page is built from real check-in and engagement data, recipients share something true and personal, extending the event's reach organically across LinkedIn and other channels.

entries.title: Portals, Sites, galleries and registration meet WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility standards
entries.summary: A comprehensive WCAG 2.2 AA remediation improves keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, colour contrast and reflow across the abstract/awards submission form, review portal, Sites, content galleries and registration. Key changes include: single- and multi-select fields use proper ARIA combobox/listbox patterns; radio questions render as real radio groups; every form field has a linked label, help text and error message; a focused **error summary** replaces the per-field toast on save; brand accent colours that failed contrast with white text now automatically switch to black text; navigation items are real links with `aria-current="page"` and keyboard support; media players expose caption tracks and a transcript link; 30 hard-coded registration strings are now translated in all six supported languages; and the portal reflows correctly at 320 px with a visible skip link and reduced-motion support.

where.path: Participant portal (submission, review, tasks, welcome); Sites → any published site; Content Galleries; Registration form

entries.use_case: Organizations serving attendees who rely on assistive technology — including universities running abstract submission programs — can now point those participants at a portal, site or gallery that meets WCAG 2.2 AA without custom workarounds. Reviewers using keyboard-only navigation can move through scorecards and filters without a mouse.

cs_action.note: Several behaviour changes are visible to all users without any toggle: radio questions now render as radio buttons (matching the admin builder preview); brand accent colours that fail 4.5:1 contrast with white now display black text instead; the 'Please fix N issues' toast on awards/session forms is replaced by a focused error summary at the top of the form; a required empty rich-text answer is now blocked on the awards form (as it already was on the session form). Review with customers who have custom brand colours or who rely on the toast UX.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about accessibility compliance, VPAT requests, or university/government procurement requirements; also when a customer reports that radio questions look different or that their brand colour changed on buttons.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — changes are default-on. Highest relevance for academic, government and healthcare customers with formal accessibility obligations.
internal.staff_path: Participant portal → any submission or review form; Sites → published site nav and gallery; Registration form
internal.gotchas: 82 of 218 live Site accent colours previously failed contrast with white text — those sites will now show black text on accent buttons and chips. The awards form now blocks submission of a required empty rich-text field (previously it silently passed). The 'Please fix N issues' toast is gone; errors appear in a focused summary banner instead. Customer images without alt text get a data-a11y-missing-alt marker visible in the DOM but not to end users — a builder warning is planned.
internal.talk_track: This release brings the participant-facing surfaces up to WCAG 2.2 AA, which means keyboard users, screen-reader users and anyone on a small screen will have a much smoother experience. For customers with accessibility procurement requirements, this is a meaningful step toward a VPAT.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/accessibility guide should be expanded to document the specific WCAG 2.2 AA improvements now in place (keyboard navigation patterns, contrast behaviour for brand colours, error summary, caption tracks on media players, and translation coverage), and note the automatic black-text fallback for low-contrast accent colours.
draft.why_use_it: Accessible registration and portal experiences let every participant — including those using screen readers, keyboard navigation, or high-contrast displays — complete submissions, review assignments and access event content on equal terms. Meeting WCAG 2.2 AA also helps organizations satisfy institutional accessibility policies and procurement requirements.

entries.title: Read Advocacy results — summary, advocates and pacing — via the Public API
entries.summary: Three new read-only endpoints expose Advocacy campaign data to connected AI assistants and API integrations: **GET /v1/event/:eventId/advocacy/summary**, **GET /v1/event/:eventId/advocacy/advocates**, and **GET /v1/event/:eventId/advocacy/pacing**. Existing Claude and ChatGPT connections using the `read:events` scope can call them immediately without reconnecting. Attendee counts are returned, not names. Restricted API keys that limit access to specific events receive a `403 EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED` response when a `compare_event_id` falls outside their allowed list.

where.path: Apps → API tokens (or connected AI assistant)

entries.use_case: Organizers who have connected Claude or ChatGPT to Sessionboard can now ask their AI assistant how an Advocacy campaign is performing — total shares, top advocates and pacing trends — without leaving the chat. Teams using the Public API directly can pull the same data into dashboards or reports.

cs_action.note: Endpoints are default-on for any event with Advocacy. No configuration required. Restricted-key customers are protected automatically by the allowlist check.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to pull Advocacy performance data into an AI assistant or external dashboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer running Advocacy campaigns who has already connected Claude, ChatGPT, or a custom API integration.
internal.staff_path: Apps → API tokens
internal.gotchas: The pacing endpoint accepts a compare_event_id parameter for cross-event comparison; API keys scoped to specific events will receive 403 EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED if the comparison event is not on their allowlist. Attendee-level PII is not exposed — only counts.
internal.talk_track: If you're already using Claude or ChatGPT with Sessionboard, you can now ask it how your Advocacy campaign is performing — shares, top advocates, pacing — without any reconnection or new token.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section listing which Advocacy data points (summary, advocates, pacing) are available through the Public API and note that the read:events scope is sufficient, including the cross-event pacing comparison parameter and its allowlist behaviour for restricted keys.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting an AI assistant to Sessionboard lets you query your event data in plain language instead of navigating reports manually. With Advocacy results now available through the API, you can ask about campaign reach, who your top advocates are, and how sharing is trending over time — all from Claude, ChatGPT, or any tool that holds an API token. The `read:events` scope that every existing connection already carries is all that is needed.

entries.title: Query Advocacy results from AI assistants and the Public API
entries.summary: Three read-only endpoints — **summary**, **advocates**, and **pacing** — expose Advocacy analytics through the Public API and connected AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini). **Summary** returns the same KPIs, funnel, channel mix, and per-campaign rows shown on **Advocacy → Analytics**. **Advocates** lists each named speaker, company contact, or team member with their share status (`shared`, `opened`, `notified`, `not_notified`), so you can ask "which speakers haven't shared yet?" Attendees are counted in aggregate and never named. **Pacing** shows daily or weekly activity relative to the event start date and supports comparing against a previous edition from the same organisation.

where.path: Advocacy → Analytics (data also accessible via Public API and connected AI assistants)

entries.use_case: Organizers who connect an AI assistant to Sessionboard can now ask natural-language questions about Advocacy performance — such as which speakers haven't shared yet, how share volume compares to last year's event, or which channels are driving the most registrations — without leaving their AI tool or opening the platform.

cs_action.note: Endpoints are additive and read-only; no existing behaviour changes. Customers need a Public API token and a connected AI assistant to use the new tools.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses or is evaluating AI assistant integrations and also runs Advocacy campaigns — especially if they ask about reporting or 'who hasn't shared yet' workflows.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively running Advocacy campaigns who have connected Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or Gemini to Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Advocacy → Analytics (same data, now also via API/MCP)
internal.gotchas: Registrations in the API response are conversions recorded on a tracked Advocacy link (matching the dashboard count), not Marketing → Results multi-touch credit — the response notes field says so. Attendee advocates are counted in aggregate only; individual attendee names are never returned. The pacing compare_event_id must belong to the same organisation or the API returns 404.
internal.talk_track: If you're already using Claude or ChatGPT with Sessionboard, you can now ask it things like 'which of my speakers haven't shared yet?' or 'how does our share pacing compare to last year?' and get answers straight from your Advocacy data.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section listing the three Advocacy tools available to AI assistants (summary, advocates, pacing), what each returns, the attendee-privacy rule, and how to use the compare_event_id parameter for edition-over-edition pacing.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting an AI assistant to Sessionboard lets you query your event data in plain language across sessions, speakers, contacts, and now Advocacy results. Instead of navigating between screens to pull numbers, you ask a question and get an answer drawn directly from the same data the platform displays. Use it to spot gaps, compare editions, and share quick status updates with your team.

entries.title: Marketing growth: subscribers, podcasts, newsletter, journeys, pacing, Voices, video, website tag, preference center, and sponsor audience links
entries.summary: Sessionboard Marketing gains a broad set of growth tools: **Sign-up Forms** and recording gates collect subscribers; **Podcasts** turns event sessions into a show with episodes, covers, and a feed; **Newsletter** drafts recap issues, schedules sends, and reports results; four fixed **Event Journeys** automate follow-up; **Turnout Pacing** tracks registration and attendance against the last edition and a goal; **Voices** collects short video responses via prompt, open link, or QR code and assembles a reel; a unified **Video Player** tracks per-person watch time with gates, end cards, and premieres; a **Website Tag** captures page visits; a **Preference Center** (`/prefs/:token`) lets subscribers manage their own preferences; and **Sponsor Audience** links (`/sponsor-audience/:token`) give sponsors a view of their audience.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Marketing; then Marketing → (each section)

where.path: Marketing → Subscribers, Podcasts, Newsletter, Journeys, Pacing, Voices, Video, Website Tag, Preferences, Sponsors

entries.use_case: An event marketing team can now grow and nurture their audience end-to-end inside Sessionboard: collect subscribers with sign-up forms, turn session recordings into a podcast and newsletter, automate post-event journeys, track registration pacing against last year, gather authentic video testimonials with Voices, gate on-demand content behind a video player, and give sponsors a direct view of their audience — all without leaving the platform.

cs_action.note: Marketing workspace must be provisioned for the org. Self-serve sign-up flags (MARKETING_SIGNUP_ENABLED) remain off; public token pages (/subscribe/:formId, /prefs/:token, /sponsor-audience/:token) are live but only respond for tokens that exist. Help links in the workspace 404 until the docs suite is released — coordinate docs release with this feature release.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to grow their audience, repurpose session content, automate post-event follow-up, or give sponsors audience data.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Marketing add-on who are actively promoting events and want to grow a subscriber base or repurpose content.
internal.staff_path: Marketing (org-level sidebar)
internal.gotchas: Merging deployed to DEV only at time of PR; web-api endpoints and migrations must be deployed first or new Marketing sections return 404s. Dark-mode, a11y, and i18n (de/es/fr) are included in this branch.
internal.talk_track: You can now collect subscribers with a sign-up form, turn your sessions into a podcast and newsletter, automate follow-up journeys, track pacing against last year's event, collect Voices video testimonials, gate on-demand video, and give sponsors their own audience link — all inside Sessionboard Marketing.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has stub pages for /sessionboard-marketing/content/podcast and /sessionboard-marketing/content/newsletter but no guides yet for Sign-up Forms/Subscribers, Event Journeys, Turnout Pacing, Voices, the unified Video Player, Website Tag, Preference Center, or Sponsor Audience links — each needs its own guide or a combined growth guide covering all GROW-1 through GROW-13 capabilities.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing connects your event content to your audience growth in one place. Use it to turn every session into a podcast episode, newsletter issue, or short video, then distribute through automated journeys and measure what drives registrations. Sponsors and exhibitors get their own audience links so you can demonstrate value without exporting data.

entries.title: Expand buttons in embedded widgets are named for what they open
entries.summary: Every **Show more** and **View Details** button in the agenda, schedule, sessions, speakers, and speaker-gallery embeds now carries a descriptive accessible name — for example, **"Show more about [session title]"** — so screen readers announce exactly which item the button expands. Labels are translated into German, French, and Spanish.

where.path: Publish → Embeds → embed code on the customer's website

entries.use_case: Organizations with accessibility requirements — public agencies, medical societies, associations — can embed their agenda or speaker list and have keyboard and screen-reader users hear a meaningful button name instead of a repeated "Show more" with no context.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about WCAG compliance for their embedded agenda or speaker list, or mentions screen-reader users on their website.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with embeds on their website, especially accessibility-conscious associations, public bodies, and medical societies.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Embeds → open the embed → copy the embed code
internal.gotchas: This is part of the ongoing WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility epic (SB-11252, round 2). No markup or attribute contract changes — existing embed codes do not need to be updated.
internal.talk_track: Every expand button in your embedded agenda and speaker list now tells screen-reader users exactly which session or speaker it opens, and the labels are translated into German, French, and Spanish.

draft.docs_gap: The embeds guide should note that expand and detail buttons carry session- or speaker-specific accessible names and are translated alongside other embed language settings.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's embedded widgets let you publish your agenda, session list, speaker gallery, and schedule directly on your own website without any custom development. Visitors can browse sessions, read speaker bios, and expand details without leaving your site. The widgets inherit your event data automatically and support multiple languages, so your public-facing program stays current with no extra effort.

entries.title: Portals and Sites meet WCAG 2.2 AA: image alt text, media transcripts, rich-text descriptions and focus fixes
entries.summary: A broad set of accessibility improvements lands across speaker portals and program sites. In the **Site Builder**, image, gallery, logo and venue blocks now carry an **Alt text** / **Decorative** option per item; images missing a description are outlined and badged in the canvas so they are easy to spot. In the **portal rich-text editor**, undescribed images are flagged below the field and a **Describe images** dialog lets you add a description or mark each image as decorative — saving is never blocked. In the gallery, lesson and reviewer **media players**, description tracks render as an in-page **Described transcript** disclosure with timed text. Additional fixes: the **Resend login link** button keeps focus after click; file-upload fields gain `aria-invalid` while an error shows; submission navigation reflows correctly at 320 px; the site **Filters** button hides on desktop as intended; a 404 site URL now shows a proper "Site not found" page instead of an endless skeleton; and 17 gallery aria-labels are translated.

where.path: Sites → Site Builder → block settings (alt text); Portal → rich-text field → Describe images; Content Gallery → media player → Described transcript

entries.use_case: Organizations with accessibility requirements — public agencies, medical societies, associations — can publish portals, program sites and content galleries that meet WCAG 2.2 AA for keyboard and screen-reader users, and satisfy procurement or legal mandates without custom workarounds.

cs_action.note: Several visible defaults changed: the site Filters button now hides on desktop (was always visible due to a CSS specificity bug); a bad site URL now shows a 'Site not found' page instead of a skeleton; submission navigation is 320 px wide at 320 px viewport (was 393 px). Customers who built CSS targeting the old skeleton or the Filters button layout may notice a difference.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about WCAG compliance, accessibility audits, or government/association procurement requirements for their portal or program site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose event portal or program site is subject to accessibility requirements, or who has received an accessibility audit finding.
internal.staff_path: Sites → Site Builder → select an image/gallery/logo/venue block → block settings panel; Portal → open a rich-text field → image icon → Describe images
internal.gotchas: The canvas alt-text badge and outline are builder-only visual aids — they do not appear to portal visitors. The 'Described transcript' disclosure appears only when a description track is present on the media item. The rich-text 'Describe images' dialog never blocks saving, so undescribed images can still be published.
internal.talk_track: Your portals and sites now meet WCAG 2.2 AA out of the box — you can add alt text to every image in the builder, fix rich-text image descriptions without leaving the editor, and offer described transcripts alongside your session recordings.

draft.docs_gap: The Site Builder guide should add a section on the new Alt text / Decorative options for image, gallery, logo and venue blocks, including the canvas badge for missing alt text and the sessionboard:site-builder-a11y event. The Portals 101 guide should document the rich-text Describe images dialog. The Content Galleries guide should document the Described transcript disclosure in the media player.
draft.why_use_it: The Site Builder, speaker portals and content galleries are the public and participant-facing surfaces of your event. Making them accessible means every attendee, speaker and reviewer — including those who use a keyboard, screen reader or zoom — can navigate, read and interact with your content. You can add descriptive alt text or mark images as decorative directly in the builder, flag and fix missing descriptions in rich-text fields, and offer timed described transcripts alongside video so your media meets the same standard as your text.

entries.title: Auto-generate captions for session and media files
entries.summary: Organizers can now trigger automatic caption generation on session content and media items. The **Generate captions** action sends the file through Deepgram and stores the result as a WebVTT track labelled "**[Language] (auto-generated)**". The **GET text-tracks** response now includes a `generation` object with `status`, `message`, `updated_at`, and `can_generate` so the UI can show progress; tracks also carry `source` and `status` fields, and only ready tracks are delivered to players.

where.path: Sessions → [session] → Files → text-tracks → Generate captions

entries.use_case: An organizer who needs captions for on-demand session recordings can trigger generation in one step instead of transcribing externally and uploading a VTT file. The platform queues the job, stores the result, and surfaces it to players automatically once ready.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about accessibility of recorded sessions, or mentions needing captions for on-demand content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer publishing session recordings who needs WCAG or ADA compliance, or who wants captions for international audiences.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → [session] → Files → text-tracks
internal.gotchas: Media items reuse the existing MEDIA_TRANSCRIBE job queue and will not double-queue if a transcript is already queued, processing, or ready. Session/submission/attendee files use a separate CONTENT_CAPTIONS job. Existing text-track rows are migrated to source=upload, status=ready.
internal.talk_track: You can now generate captions directly on any session recording or uploaded file — Sessionboard sends it through Deepgram and stores the WebVTT track automatically, so you don't need a separate transcription tool.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new POST …/text-tracks/generate endpoint, the generation status fields returned by GET …/text-tracks, and the presigned upload path for VTT/SRT/TXT files (POST …/text-tracks/presign).
draft.why_use_it: Captions make recorded sessions accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing attendees and improve comprehension for non-native speakers. Generating them directly from Sessionboard removes the need for a separate transcription service and manual upload. The generation status is visible in real time so organizers know when tracks are ready. Only completed tracks are delivered to video players, keeping the viewer experience clean.

entries.title: Reviewers get a dedicated home page on the Site, and the builder gains a "View as Invited guest" preview
entries.summary: Signed-in reviewers now land on a **Reviewer Home** instead of the nominee home. It shows a greeting, how many reviews remain, the next round due (round, program, deadline), a **Continue reviewing** button, their assigned rounds with progress and instructions, and a **How scoring works** four-step guide. Reviewers who also submit see a **See open programs** link to switch to the nominee home. In the Site builder, organizers can now choose **View as Invited guest** to preview how an invite-only event page appears to someone who has been invited but is not signed in.

where.path: Awards → Site → (published Site, signed in as a reviewer) and Awards → Site → Site builder → View as → Invited guest

entries.use_case: Programs with a dedicated reviewer pool no longer need to configure a widget to give reviewers a useful landing page — every reviewer arrives at a page tailored to their work. Organizers can also verify exactly what an invited-but-not-signed-in guest sees on a restricted event page without leaving the builder.

cs_action.note: The showMyReviewsHome widget flag no longer controls the reviewer home — every reviewer now gets the new Reviewer Home regardless of that setting. Customers who relied on that widget to keep reviewers on the nominee home will see a behaviour change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why reviewers are landing on a different page, or when setting up a new awards program with a reviewer panel.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Awards Site with a reviewer panel.
internal.staff_path: Awards → Site → open the published site as a reviewer account
internal.gotchas: The showMyReviewsHome widget flag is now ignored for routing; it no longer switches reviewers to the nominee home. Reviewers who also submit still see a 'See open programs' link to reach the nominee home.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers now land on a page built for them — their pending reviews, deadlines, and a scoring guide — so they can get straight to work. You can preview exactly what they see in the builder with 'View as Reviewer'.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Reviewer Home (its sections, the Continue reviewing button, and the See open programs link for dual-role users) and the new "View as Invited guest" builder persona.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard Awards Site gives reviewers, nominees, and guests a single branded destination for your awards program. Reviewers see their outstanding work and deadlines the moment they sign in, so they spend less time hunting for their assignments. Organizers can preview the site as any persona — nominee, reviewer, or invited guest — to confirm the right content appears before publishing.

entries.title: Add, generate and manage captions on videos across Media, Sessions, Academy and Learning
entries.summary: A **Captions & Transcript** panel is now available on Media items, session Files, Content Gallery items, Academy lessons and Learning courses. From the panel you can upload **.vtt**, **.srt** or **.txt** caption tracks, set a default track, delete tracks, and trigger **Generate captions** with live progress polling. Publishing a gallery, Academy draft or Learning course that contains an uncaptioned video shows a warning (publishing is never blocked). Attendee file previews, Marketing previews and the Academy lesson player render tracks automatically.

where.path: Sessions → Files → row menu or detail sidebar → Captions & Transcript; Media library → item → Captions & Transcript; Content Galleries → item → Captions & Transcript; Academy / Learning → lesson or course → Captions & Transcript

entries.use_case: Organizations with accessibility requirements — public agencies, medical societies, associations — can caption every video in their program without leaving Sessionboard, satisfying WCAG 2.2 AA and accreditor mandates for captioned continuing-education content.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about accessibility compliance, captioning for CE credit, or making on-demand video content accessible.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer publishing video through session files, content galleries, Academy or Learning — especially those with accessibility or accreditation requirements.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Files → row menu → Captions & Transcript
internal.gotchas: Generate captions requires the web-api round-2 presign endpoint; on older API deployments the panel falls back to inline text upload only. Publishing warns on uncaptioned videos but never blocks.
internal.talk_track: You can now upload or auto-generate captions on every video in your program — session files, galleries, Academy lessons and Learning courses — and attendees see them automatically in the player.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining the Captions & Transcript panel: how to upload .vtt/.srt/.txt files, set a default track, delete tracks, and use Generate captions with progress polling.
draft.why_use_it: Captions make video content accessible to attendees who are deaf or hard of hearing, support non-native speakers, and satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA requirements that many public and professional organizations must meet. Upload your own caption files or let Sessionboard generate them, then set a default track so attendees always see captions without extra steps. The same tracks appear in the attendee file preview, Marketing content previews and the Academy lesson player.

entries.title: Site builder publish diff no longer flags unchanged defaults as edits
entries.summary: The **Publish** dialog and version history in the Site builder no longer list **Accent colour changed**, **Text colour changed**, or **Events directory changed** when those settings were never touched. Previously, a site that had never set these values showed them as changed on the very first autosave because the builder's defaults were compared against empty database values.

where.path: Sites → [site] → Site builder → Publish

entries.use_case: Organizers who open the Site builder for the first time and immediately publish will see a clean, accurate change summary — only the edits they actually made are listed, making it easier to audit what changed between versions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their site version history shows colour or Events directory changes they never made.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Site builder, especially those who recently opened a new site for the first time.
internal.staff_path: Sites → [site] → Site builder → Publish → review the diff list; also visible in version history summaries and via the get_site_diff MCP/Ask tool.
internal.gotchas: The fix also normalises hex colour comparisons case- and length-blind (#FFF = #ffffff), so previously logged 'changes' that were only case differences will also stop appearing going forward.
internal.talk_track: The publish diff now only shows changes you actually made — opening the builder and autosaving without touching colours or the Events directory will no longer create a noisy history entry.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the publish diff and version history reflect only real edits, and that default values for accent colour, text colour, light/dark mode, Brand Kit follow, and the Events directory are treated as equivalent to an unset state.

entries.title: Keyboard focus returns correctly after closing dialogs and switching views in the reviewer portal
entries.summary: Two WCAG 2.2 AA focus-order fixes in the speaker/reviewer portal: closing the **Sign in to vote** dialog now returns keyboard focus to the button that opened it (instead of dropping to the page body), and switching from the reviewer home view to **See open programs** moves focus to that view's heading so screen-reader and keyboard users land in the right place. A **Back to my reviews** button lets reviewers switch back, returning focus to **See open programs**.

where.path: Portal → Reviewer home → See open programs / Sign in to vote dialog

entries.use_case: Organizations with accessibility requirements (public agencies, medical societies, associations) can point keyboard and screen-reader users to the portal's voting and review flows without those users losing their place after closing a dialog or switching views.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that keyboard or screen-reader users lose focus after closing the vote login dialog or switching views on the reviewer home page, or when an accessibility audit flags SC 2.4.3 Focus Order on the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose attendees or reviewers use keyboards or assistive technology to navigate the portal.
internal.staff_path: Portal → Reviewer home
internal.gotchas: Fix applies to the new portals (new_portals feature); legacy portals are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: Keyboard and screen-reader users no longer lose their place when they close the vote dialog or switch between reviewer views — focus goes exactly where it should.

draft.docs_gap: The portals guide should note that the portal meets WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.4.3 Focus Order for dialogs and view switches, and describe the Back to my reviews button available to reviewers.

entries.title: Time quizzes, draw from a question bank, and score written answers in the course builder
entries.summary: Three new course-authoring capabilities are available in the Learning course builder. Set a **Time limit** on any quiz and grant individual learners **Extra time**. Open the **Question bank** sheet to search, tag, add, edit, archive and restore reusable questions; insert them into a lesson with **/ Questions from the bank** or save any question with **Save to question bank**. Under **Approvals → Answers to score**, award points, leave notes, and see a live pass/fail preview for written-answer and file questions.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Lessons

where.path: Learning → course builder → quiz block (time limit); Learning → course builder → slash menu → Questions from the bank; Learning → Approvals → Answers to score

entries.use_case: Training teams that need to certify learners can enforce time-boxed assessments, reuse a vetted question library across multiple courses, and manually grade open-ended answers — all without leaving the course builder.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about timed exams, reusable question libraries, or grading open-ended quiz answers in Learning.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessionboard Learning who run certification programs, compliance training, or any course that requires scored assessments.
internal.staff_path: Learning → course builder → quiz block settings; Learning → Approvals → Answers to score
internal.gotchas: All three capabilities are inside the self-serve Learning workspace and are gated behind the Lessons preview feature; no Platform screen changes were made.
internal.talk_track: You can now set a countdown timer on any quiz, give individual learners extra time for accommodations, pull questions from a shared bank so you don't rewrite them for every course, and grade written answers with a structured scoring panel.

draft.docs_gap: The timed-quizzes guide exists but should cross-link to the new question-bank and score-written-answers guides; the question-bank guide should document the slash-menu insertion flow and the Save to question bank option on individual questions.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard Learning course builder lets you author structured courses with quizzes, timed assessments, and manually graded questions in one place. Timed quizzes add exam-like conditions to any quiz block, with per-learner accommodation controls. The question bank lets you maintain a single library of vetted questions and pull them into any course, keeping assessments consistent as content evolves. Written-answer scoring gives instructors a structured review queue with points, notes, and a live pass preview so grading is fast and auditable.

entries.title: Report PDFs name each record, and subscribe-gate playback exposes captions
entries.summary: In report PDFs that contain related sections, each record's heading now identifies the record — for example **"Submission: ABS-1042"** — and related-table captions carry the same name, e.g. **"Co-authors — ABS-1042"**. Screen-reader users can distinguish repeated headings and tables. Separately, the subscribe-gate video playback now returns **captions** and **transcript_url** fields so caption tracks that were already uploaded appear on the gated player.

where.path: Reports → open a report → Download PDF

entries.use_case: Organizations with accessibility requirements (public agencies, medical societies, associations) can share report PDFs with screen-reader users who need to navigate between records. Events using gated video can now surface caption tracks to viewers who rely on them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer mentions accessibility of exported reports, or asks why captions are missing on their subscribe-gate player.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who exports report PDFs with related sections, or who uses subscribe-gate video with caption tracks uploaded.
internal.staff_path: Reports → open a report with related sections → Download PDF; for captions, the gate playback is on the content gallery or marketing page.
internal.gotchas: Record names in PDFs use the first non-empty field as plain text; a record with no values falls back to a positional label like 'Submission 3'. Caption fields are additive — existing integrations are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: Report PDFs now label each record so screen-reader users can tell them apart, and caption tracks you've already uploaded now appear on your gated video player.

draft.docs_gap: The report-builder guide should document that downloaded PDFs name each record in headings and related-table captions, and note the fallback label when a record has no field values.
